selection_rule: Choose the spatial composition from carrier, information structure, and intended reading behavior before resolving the subject. The subject must fit the selected object slot; it must not determine the layout.

selection_flow.when: The user explicitly requests a composition
An editorial poster is led by facts, schedule, method, classification, or 2–4 support elements
The phrase itself is the primary image or declaration
One subject repeats as a collection, sequence, inventory, or rhythm
A supplied portrait, photograph, or scene must remain recognizable
The idea depends on entry, enclosure, aperture, portal, or architectural framing
The idea depends on direction, transit, projection, navigation, or one vanishing vector
One iconic isolated subject benefits from a calm frontal or axial presentation

global_contract.attention_definition: Perceptual attention at thumbnail size, not literal pixel area.
global_contract.title_rule: The title remains the dominant reading event. Do not shrink it to preserve the full subject.
global_contract.support_rule: Support copy occupies only named structural anchors; never scatter decorative pseudo-data.
global_contract.event_rule: Select exactly one focal event. Every other energetic element extends it or releases it.
global_contract.release_rule: Reserve one visibly quieter region with lower contrast, detail, and information density.
global_contract.object_slot_rule: Resolve the subject only after composition. Crop, scale, orient, repeat, or fragment it to satisfy the object slot while preserving identity anchors.

layouts.name: Asymmetric Counterweight
layouts.select_when: One dominant subject and one title block can balance across unequal regions without a centered product presentation.
layouts.dominant_mass: title first; one subject mass acts as the counterweight
layouts.title_zone: the broad counter-space opposite or diagonally adjacent to the subject mass
layouts.object_slot: one large side-biased mass; complete or edge-cropped according to scale role
layouts.collision_rule: title and subject share one edge, tangent, or shaped counter-space; they do not float as unrelated halves
layouts.crop_rule: crop one or two outer edges when the subject exceeds 36% of the canvas; protect 2–4 identity anchors
layouts.title_relationship: counterbalances or presses against the subject without covering its identity anchors
layouts.object_behavior: large and materially specific; the object adapts to the side-biased slot
layouts.release_zone: the largest region opposite the subject mass or inside unused title-line counter-space
layouts.thumbnail_test: title reads first and the unequal counterweight relationship is visible before details

layouts.name: Centered Anchor
layouts.select_when: One iconic subject, symbol, or device benefits from a calm axial presentation while the title and metadata remain dominant.
layouts.dominant_mass: large title plus one compact central anchor
forbidden_relationships: several equal satellites around the center
layouts.title_zone: centered above, below, or split around the anchor on one vertical axis
layouts.object_slot: one intact or selectively cropped subject centered on a baseline, horizon, pedestal, or disc
layouts.collision_rule: title may overlap a low-detail portion of the anchor or split around it; never cover its recognition anchors
layouts.crop_rule: default to an intact silhouette; use one controlled bottom or side crop only when monumental scale is selected
layouts.title_relationship: shares the centerline with the subject and remains perceptually larger
layouts.object_behavior: compact, iconic, and explicitly grounded; never an ungrounded floating product render
layouts.release_zone: one broad upper or lower field outside the central title-object stack
failure_signals: floating object with no horizon or baseline
all metadata stacked in the center
layouts.thumbnail_test: the title remains first while the centered subject reads as one unmistakable anchor

layouts.name: Frame Threshold
layouts.select_when: The concept depends on entry, enclosure, aperture, portal, screen, hatch, or an architectural boundary.
layouts.dominant_mass: title and frame form the primary system; subject occupies or approaches the opening
forbidden_relationships: objects scattered outside the threshold system
frame used as an unrelated decorative card
layouts.title_zone: beside, across, or partially inside one low-detail opening
layouts.object_slot: one subject at the threshold, inside the frame, or cropped by the boundary
layouts.collision_rule: title approaches or enters one opening while readable glyph silhouettes stay clear
layouts.crop_rule: the frame may leave the canvas on one or two sides; do not show a complete decorative portal floating in the center
required_structure: no second portal or orbit system
layouts.title_relationship: aligns to the opening, frame tangent, or threshold axis
layouts.object_behavior: occupies, crosses, or approaches one frame; never decorates a separate empty frame
layouts.release_zone: inside or immediately beside the opening, kept low contrast behind copy
failure_signals: frame used as a UI card
layouts.thumbnail_test: one opening and one entry direction remain obvious after details disappear

layouts.name: Perspective Vector
layouts.select_when: Direction, transit, projection, navigation, velocity, or spatial construction is essential to the idea.
layouts.dominant_mass: title follows or resists one directional field; subject sits on the same vector
layouts.title_zone: on the open side of the perspective field or aligned to one fold
layouts.object_slot: one object or fragment placed on, emerging from, or countering the vector
layouts.collision_rule: title, subject, and support copy share one vanishing direction; no independent second line system
layouts.crop_rule: crop along the vector or at the foreground edge; preserve a readable directional silhouette
required_structure: one plane, shard field, or folded grid
one object slot on the vector
layouts.title_relationship: shares one directional axis, fold, or aligned corner with the spatial field
layouts.object_behavior: one structural object or fragment; never a complete explanatory sci-fi scene
layouts.release_zone: the open horizon or low-density side of the directional field
layouts.thumbnail_test: one directional thrust and one dominant title block remain legible

layouts.name: Rhythmic Field
layouts.select_when: One subject family must read as a collection, sequence, repeated signal, inventory, or packaging rhythm.
layouts.dominant_mass: title plus one repeated family; one instance owns the focal scale
layouts.title_zone: one protected band, gap, or corner left open by the repetition
layouts.object_slot: 2–5 instances from one subject family with varied scale, crop, or angle
layouts.collision_rule: title touches at most one contour; repeated instances establish rhythm rather than surrounding every line
layouts.crop_rule: at least one instance may crop at an edge; one largest instance remains the visual anchor
required_structure: one coherent path or grid rhythm
layouts.title_relationship: locks to the open zone created by the repeated path
layouts.object_behavior: repeats one family only; variation comes from scale, crop, spacing, and angle
layouts.release_zone: one visibly quieter band or corner with no extra copies
layouts.thumbnail_test: the field reads as one family with one dominant instance, not decorative wallpaper

layouts.name: Type Dominant Field
layouts.select_when: The phrase, claim, or title is the primary visual subject and the physical subject is optional or subordinate.
layouts.dominant_mass: title is the unmistakable largest mass
layouts.title_zone: a central, side, or vertical block occupying the primary field
layouts.object_slot: one small-to-medium counterweight at a title edge, corner, baseline, or internal counter-space
layouts.collision_rule: the subject interrupts one title edge or occupies unused line-shaped space; it never becomes a second hero
layouts.crop_rule: crop type only when the remaining word is immediately inferable; crop the subject only to support the same typographic event
required_structure: one subordinate physical or atmospheric interruption
layouts.title_relationship: title controls the page; every other element supports its scale, contour, or axis
layouts.object_behavior: small to medium and subordinate; may be omitted when type alone carries the idea
layouts.release_zone: one broad field around or between title lines with low information density
failure_signals: title and object have equal weight
cropped word is no longer inferable
layouts.thumbnail_test: the title shape is the first and largest recognizable event

layouts.name: Image Mask Field
layouts.select_when: A supplied portrait, scene, photograph, or image-derived fragment must remain recognizable while supporting a title-dominant cover.
layouts.dominant_mass: title first; one image field provides the narrative surface
forbidden_relationships: identity anchors divided across unrelated focal zones
mask used as a UI card
layouts.title_zone: one exposed, faded, or low-detail cut inside or beside the image field
layouts.object_slot: one recognizable image field, portrait fragment, or scene crop preserving 2–4 identity anchors
layouts.collision_rule: title overlaps a low-detail image region or occupies a shaped mask; never cover the primary identity anchor
layouts.crop_rule: crop decisively for title hierarchy while retaining 2–4 identity anchors; intrinsic text is preserved when identity-bearing and subordinate
required_structure: paper or atmosphere entering the image
layouts.title_relationship: overlaps, cuts into, or locks tightly to the image field while preserving recognition
layouts.object_behavior: cropped, graded, screened, or symbol-extracted according to source mode
layouts.release_zone: one image-free or low-detail shaped region large enough for the title
layouts.thumbnail_test: title reads first and the supplied subject remains identifiable without the caption

layouts.name: Information Axis
layouts.select_when: An editorial poster must carry 5–7 truthful text elements such as a title, deck, date, location, index, classification, or footer.
layouts.dominant_mass: title remains first; factual support copy becomes the structural skeleton
forbidden_relationships: support copy detached from the information rule
equal hierarchy between title and factual clusters
layouts.title_zone: one large block intersecting or sharing a rule with the factual system
layouts.object_slot: one specimen, fragment, or counterweight attached to the same rule or grid
layouts.collision_rule: headline, object, and facts share one explicit axis; rules organize information rather than decorate the page
layouts.crop_rule: the subject may crop against the information axis; text never crops and factual strings remain legible
required_structure: one primary information rule or grid
one subject attached to the same system
layouts.title_relationship: crosses or shares the primary rule while remaining at least one clear scale tier above factual copy
layouts.object_behavior: acts as a specimen, crop, or counterweight attached to the information system; never as an unrelated hero render
layouts.release_zone: one open reading field between title, specimen, and factual clusters
failure_signals: decorative rules with no alignment job
layouts.thumbnail_test: the title reads first, the information axis reads second, and the support copy collapses into one coherent system
